key_insight: DK-VLM improves spatial reasoning in vision-language models by treating geometry as a position signal, not just extra features. Its Dual-Kernel Attention helps the model better align 3D scene structure with pretrained semantic knowledge, especially when viewpoint changes.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty vision-language models have in understanding 3D spatial relationships across different views and updating those judgments as the observer moves. It also tackles the alignment gap between reconstructed geometric features and semantic visual tokens when spatial supervision is limited.
method: Introduces Dual-Kernel Attention to combine two sources of position information: a token's original visual position and its geometric position in the reconstructed scene.
Fuses 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens while preserving compatibility with pretrained semantic representations.
Uses geometry-aware attention to strengthen spatial reasoning across viewpoints and improve robustness under sparse spatial supervision.
impact: This matters for practitioners building embodied AI, robotics, and multimodal systems that need reliable 3D scene understanding. It offers a practical direction for improving spatial reasoning without relying on large amounts of explicit spatial annotation.

paper_title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
